faq.q: Is Auserene better than Day One?
faq.a: If you want a journal that does something with your day, yes. Auserene connects quick notes, an evening conversation, a meditation made from your day, memory you can read and edit, people and habit goals. Day One is the better pick for a long photo and video archive, print books, end-to-end encryption, or Android, Windows and the web.

Yes, on the Gold plan. Day One's AI features include Daily Chat, Go Deeper prompts, entry highlights, title suggestions, image generation and summaries. Daily Chat uses OpenAI, and some features can run on-device with Apple Intelligence. In Auserene, the AI conversation is the center of the app, and it also writes a meditation from your day.

faq.q: What is Day One Daily Chat?
faq.a: Daily Chat is Day One's AI conversation feature. It asks questions about your day and turns the conversation into a journal entry you can edit. It builds memories of your routines and relationships, but Day One says you can't review or delete individual memories in its iPhone, iPad or Mac apps. Auserene lists every memory in plain sentences you can edit or delete.

faq.q: How much is Day One Gold?
faq.a: Day One Gold costs $74.99 a year in the US as of November 2026. Silver costs $49.99 a year, and Basic is free. Day One offers a one-month free trial in the app. A monthly Gold price isn't listed on its pricing page. Auserene Premium is $11.99 a month or $105.99 a year, with seven days free.

faq.q: Is Day One Gold worth it?
faq.a: If you already use Day One and want Daily Chat and AI summaries, Gold costs $25 a year more than Silver and keeps everything Silver has. If you want memory you can review on iPhone, mood tracking, meditation, people or habit goals, Gold doesn't list them, and Auserene has all five.

faq.q: Is Day One still end-to-end encrypted if I use AI?
faq.a: Day One offers end-to-end encryption on every plan. Its AI guide says content from end-to-end encrypted journals is temporarily not end-to-end encrypted while being processed by AI, and that content isn't used to train AI models. Auserene isn't end-to-end encrypted; the AI that reads your journal works under zero-data-retention terms and is contractually barred from training on your words.
